changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard forms (e.g., 'GPT-4' instead of 'gpt-4'), but kept all existing items as they are correctly extracted and relevant.

Consolidated metric variations (e.g., 'Correct Path Rate' instead of 'CP%', 'Error Rate' instead of 'Error'). Removed specific NDCG variants as they are covered by the base 'NDCG' metric. Added 'Correct Path Rate' which is the main metric mentioned for RestBench evaluation.

Consolidated redundant method descriptions and removed overly specific hallucination criteria which are implementation details rather than evaluation criteria. Kept the core evaluation criteria mentioned in the paper.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated criteria by removing redundant entries and normalizing to core criteria. The key human evaluation focuses on error identification (tool name/parameter errors) and quality assessment (correctness/plausibility) of the generated tool instructions.

overall_notes: The extraction quality is generally good. The paper focuses on tool utilization and instruction generation for LLM-based agents, which involves natural language generation aspects. All evaluations (automatic metrics, LLM-as-judge, human evaluation) are well-documented in the paper. The human evaluations are extensive with multiple annotators and inter-annotator agreement scores reported.
